name: concepts-readroom-explore/shells
refs: THE POD (project-owned game art): a wild seed pod, slate-blue with a round coral cap, pale vertical ribs and coral dots, standing on a small turned wooden dish. Keep its design exactly wherever the pod appears; never make it a jar, a vase, a lantern of metal, or an egg of another design.

THE CREATURE (project-owned game art): the Loika the pod will become: a small round charcoal creature with a cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, four stubby legs with pale toes and three green leaves on its head. Keep its design exactly; never invent another creature.

THE PAINTED LANGUAGE (one of our signed Vivarium room paintings, project-owned): its matte painterly miniature rendering, soft occlusion, warm golden light, cosy palette. Take the treatment and the warmth only, none of its objects.
prompt:
Paint the WHOLE screen of a cosy handheld creature-keeping game, 16:9, a mood-and-layout thumbnail for a concept: the READING ROOM, where the player opens up a wild pod (a seed pod with a creature's genome sleeping inside) one surprise at a time. The feeling: a pod is RICH IN SURPRISES, there is more inside than you can see, and each read brings one out into the light. CONCEPT: THE SHELLS. The pod opens like a nest of shells, one inside another, and every shell lifted shows the next painted surprise, down to the creature at the heart. COMPOSITION: on a warm wooden table at evening, big and centred, the pod stands OPEN: its top half (coral cap, slate-blue ribs) lifted and held up by an unseen hand at the top right, and inside it a smaller inner shell of a different warm colour, also open, and inside that a smaller one, like nesting shells, five rings in all seen in cross-section, each ring's inner face painted with a soft picture: russet fur on the outer, an amber eye on the next, pale toes, a leaf, a curl of tail, going inward and brighter. At the very heart, tiny and glowing, the Loika curled asleep in warm light, fully in colour. Two lifted shells already lie on the table to the left, face up, their pictures showing. Soft dust motes in the lamp light. A dark warm study wall behind.
LIGHT AND FINISH: warm key light, warm bounce, soft ambient occlusion, soft contact shadows. Matte, hand-painted miniature finish like the painted reference, cosy and warm, real depth; low saturation everywhere except the pod's inner light and the surprises. No gloss, no chrome, no plastic, no neon, no sci-fi interface, no holograms, nothing childish.
NO text, letters, digits, numbers, logos, buttons, panels, boxes or icons anywhere (the game types its words later). No frame, no border, no vignette; the picture fills the canvas edge to edge.
